identity.real_world_identity_notes: A specialist dossier for the surviving period FIA GT chassis specifies a Tractive six-speed sequential gearbox. AMS2 visibly models a sequential lever without paddles. The exact year/chassis specification represented remains qualified.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a D-shaped rim without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car stalled when moving from rest without physical clutch input.
All six sequential-stick gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts with perceptible automatic cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted and no automatic throttle blip was observed; authentic rev matching therefore requires the driver to blip the throttle manually.

PMR's official car page and its 2004-spec article identify the Gillet Vertigo and its 2004 specification. OverTake's contemporary report identifies the game car as the 2004 Gillet Vertigo Streiff, and Racing Sports Cars records the exact chassis YA9VA2900Y0169021 at the 2004 Spa 24 Hours as a Gillet Vertigo Streiff. The same chassis is the surviving FIA-GT car described by RaceArt, whose current dossier specifies a Tractive six-speed sequential gearbox. These sources bridge the abbreviated PMR telemetry name to the existing curated record without treating the simulator controls as real-car evidence.
